newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end up, off high on rate rise report.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end up, off high on rate rise report.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended up on Monday, but came off the day's highs on a U.S. news agency report quoting a senior LDP official as saying a rise in the official discount rate will be considered after general elections.
"JGBs were falling sharply due to the news agency report," said a brokerage trader.
After having been sold suddenly after the report appeared, however, JGBs have been bought back somewhat, the trader said.
The December ended bid-only at 123.05, up sharply from Friday's 122.83.

Shizuka Kamei, the Liberal Democratic Party's publicity chief, was quoted as saying that a rise in Japan's official discount rate, and other interest rates, may be considered after the October 20 general election.
Asked about the report, a Bank of Japan official said the central bank does not comment on such issues every time they emerge.
The December skyrocketed to above 123.00 earlier in the day, due to short-covering after the release of surprisingly weak U.S. September employment data on Friday, traders said.
The December set a record high for any futures contract at 123.45 in the morning session.

U.S. non-farm payrolls shrank by 40,000 in September, marking the first decrease since January. The data eliminated much of the market's expectations that the Fed will raise rates in the near future, dealers said.
Japan's August machinery orders data, due on Tuesday, is not expected to have much impact on the market, traders said.
The market is expecting about an eight percent month-on- month decline in machinery orders for August, they said.
"Under current market conditions I don't think JGBs will be sold that much even if the figures come out pretty strong," said a city bank dealer.
Relatively strong demand is expected for twenty-year JGBs to be offered through an auction on Tuesday, traders said.
"I heard a lot of people say they expect strong demand for the twenty-year JGBs at the auction," a trust bank trader said.
The coupon rate for the twenty-year JGBs is expected to be around 3.5 percent, traders said.
